clue.text: That chap going to pub in dress bewildered country workers

indicators.note: someone bewildered is confused and muddled, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled
the first pieces sit inside the reworked letters, so 'in' tells us to place one within the other

blocks.note: the pronoun for that chap
PH is the map abbreviation for public house
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A man heading to the pub in a dress leaves the farm labourers baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress' looks like clothing the chap is wearing, but it is only letters to scramble, split around the inserted pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Shepherds tend sheep out on the land, so they are rural labourers by trade.

clue.text: Expectations from booths surrounding a road

indicators.note: surrounding means going all the way round, so one piece encloses the others

blocks.note: stalls or booths at a fair or market
taken as written
RD is the usual abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: Visitors to a roadside row of stalls arrive with certain hopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Standards are the levels of quality people require, much like the benchmarks they anticipate being met.

clue.text: Guarantees criticisms will see leader ousted

indicators.note: the leader is the opening letter, and ousting it throws that letter out of the word

blocks.note: censures are formal rebukes or criticisms

explanation.surface: A party leader is toppled after a wave of criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure something is to make certain of it, the verb sense of guaranteeing an outcome.

clue.text: Quiet American seen between rugby posts

indicators.note: being seen between two things means sitting inside them, flanked on both sides

blocks.note: rugby goalposts are shaped like the letter H, so a pair gives two of them
US is the standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A softly spoken American stands between the goalposts at a rugby match.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby posts are H-shaped, so two posts give an H on each side of US.
explanation.definitionFit: Hush means silence or stillness, and it also works as an adjective-like interjection calling for silence.

clue.text: Reduce amount of study after daughter leaves, adopting new state of existence

indicators.note: when someone leaves they are gone, so that letter is removed
adopting means taking in and housing, so the remaining letters take another inside them

blocks.note: to study less is to read less
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A student cuts back on revision once their daughter moves out, settling into a new way of life.
explanation.walkthrough: READ LESS loses its D to become REALESS, which then takes N into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Realness is the quality of being real, that is, of actually existing rather than being imagined.

clue.text: Nurse is mostly tough on the outside

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the following word is dropped
being on the outside means wrapping round, so the shortened word encloses the other piece

blocks.note: stern means strict or tough
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nurse comes across as hard-edged but is softer underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a sister is a senior nurse in charge of a ward.

clue.text: Increasingly precise printer program? Not very

indicators.note: 'not very' asks for the abbreviation of very to be absent from the word

blocks.note: a driver is the software that runs a printer
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A techie wonders whether some printer software is really all that exact.
explanation.walkthrough: DRIVER without its V leaves DRIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry can mean exact and unembellished, so the comparative form describes something growing more matter-of-fact and strict.

clue.text: More than one American shop carpet’s ripped when detective comes around

indicators.note: to come around something is to circle it, so these letters enclose the rest

blocks.note: a carpet is a rug, with the 's read as a plural
ripped means tore
DS is a detective sergeant

explanation.surface: A detective turns up to investigate a torn carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in carpet's is a decoy: it simply makes RUGS.
explanation.definitionFit: A drugstore is the US term for a pharmacy that also sells general goods, so the plural covers several such outlets.

clue.text: Junior employees playing tennis with director at last

indicators.note: playing suggests movement and rearrangement, so the letters are mixed up
at last points to the final letter of the preceding word

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
the final letter of director

explanation.surface: Office juniors join the boss for a game of tennis at the end of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Interns are trainees or newly placed workers at the bottom of an organisation.

clue.text: Communist papers further edited?

definitions.note: the question mark flags a loose definition: editing again is redoing

blocks.note: a Red is a Communist
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: Party documents from a Communist get another round of revisions.
explanation.definitionFit: Redid means did over again, and going back over a text is one example of that.

clue.text: Article suggests removing old parts of churches

indicators.note: removing means taking away, so that letter is cut out of the word

blocks.note: the indefinite article
to pose a question is to suggest it
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece proposes tearing out historic sections of church buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: Apses are the semicircular recesses usually at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Idiot jumped, striking head, being attacked

definitions.note: a participle phrase; the answer is the past participle

indicators.note: striking off the head means removing the first letter

blocks.note: an ass is a fool
vaulted means leapt over

explanation.surface: A fool leaps up and bangs his head while under attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking head' sounds like a blow to the skull; it means lose the first letter of VAULTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Assaulted means set upon violently, the same as having been attacked.

clue.text: Wretched area involved in most of Bond film

indicators.note: most of means not all, so the last letter goes
being involved in something means being caught up inside it

blocks.note: Dr No was the first James Bond film
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A miserable setting features in a large part of a 007 movie.
explanation.walkthrough: DR NO loses its O to DRN, and A goes between D and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Darn is a mild curse word used as an adjective for something annoying or wretched.

clue.text: Translation of second rune available to read

indicators.note: a translation renders words in a different form, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A scholar's version of a second runic inscription is now open to readers.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncensored text has had nothing cut, so it is fully open for anyone to read.

clue.text: Cosy places? No agreement to occupy one first to last

indicators.note: moving the first letter to the last position rotates the word
to occupy a place is to sit inside it, so these go within the other word

blocks.note: single means one
taken as written
OK signals agreement

explanation.surface: A dispute breaks out over whether a single spot can be comfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: The rotation happens first; the two short words then sit inside the rotated word, not the original.
explanation.definitionFit: An inglenook is a snug corner beside a big open fireplace, a classic warm, comfortable spot.

clue.text: Right remains in control of Nationalist Society, leading to impulsive behaviour

indicators.note: being in control of something is holding it, so this word takes the next inside it

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
ashes are what remains after burning
N is the abbreviation for Nationalist
S is the abbreviation for Society

explanation.surface: A right-wing faction takes over a nationalist group, and recklessness follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Rashness is acting hastily without thinking, a reckless kind of conduct.

clue.text: A pretentious type returned one sort of tree

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is written backwards

blocks.note: a snob is a pretentious person
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A snob goes back to buying a particular kind of tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonsai is a miniature potted tree, kept small by the Japanese art of pruning.

clue.text: I will say supporter is ignoring the law

blocks.note: I'll is the contraction of I will
e.g., for example, is another way of saying 'say'
an ally is a supporter

explanation.surface: Someone vows to back a friend who is flouting the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like speech; here it means for example, giving EG.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something illegally means acting outside or in defiance of the statutes.

clue.text: Disney film profitable around Northern part of the globe

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the first word wraps round the next letter

blocks.note: a fat contract is a lucrative one
N is the abbreviation for Northern
Asia is a continent

explanation.surface: A lucrative Disney release does well across the northern hemisphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantasia is the 1940 Disney animated feature set to classical music.

clue.text: Farm tool out of condition, left half unused

indicators.note: half unused means half of the word is left out, so only its first half is kept

blocks.note: unwell, not in good shape
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old farm implement is in poor shape, half of it never used.
explanation.definitionFit: A sickle is a curved hand blade for cutting grain or grass.

clue.text: Is accordingly entering container, a watertight container

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so these letters are placed within the other word

blocks.note: a can is a tin container
taken as written
so means therefore, accordingly

explanation.surface: Something is duly placed inside a container that keeps the water out.
explanation.definitionFit: A caisson is a sealed chamber used for underwater building work, keeping water out of the site.

clue.text: We’re off, taking trip around - arrivederci!

indicators.note: off suggests being disturbed or gone wrong, so the letters before it are jumbled
around means surrounding, so the second word encloses the jumbled letters

blocks.note: to trip is to stumble, and a trip is a fall
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers set off on a journey with an Italian goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We're off' reads as a cry of departure, which suits the definition, but 'off' is only the scrambling signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrivederci is Italian for goodbye, and farewell is the English equivalent parting word.

clue.text: Remoter regions of old city swinging both ways in middle of Texas

indicators.note: the middle of a word means its central letters, dropping the ends
in tells us one set of letters sits inside the other

blocks.note: the inner letters of Texas
Ur was an ancient city in Mesopotamia
bi means bisexual, attracted to both sexes

explanation.surface: In the heart of Texas an ancient city sways back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swinging both ways' looks like a reversal signal but is slang for bisexual, giving BI.
explanation.definitionFit: Exurbia is the prosperous belt of country beyond the suburbs, further out from the city.

clue.text: Military police officer departs during summary

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so this letter sits inside the other word

blocks.note: a recap is a brief summary
D is the abbreviation for departs on timetables

explanation.surface: A military policeman leaves partway through a briefing.
explanation.walkthrough: Redcap is British slang for a military policeman, from the red cap covers they wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcap is the nickname for a member of the Royal Military Police, named after their scarlet headgear.

clue.text: Associations? Man tingles excitedly

indicators.note: excitement sets things in agitated motion, so the letters are stirred up

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A question about relationships, answered by a man feeling a thrill.
explanation.definitionFit: Alignments are alliances or affiliations, such as a country lining up with a bloc.

clue.text: A grant to bring in river warning signal

indicators.note: to bring something in is to take it inside, so the word encloses the next letter

blocks.note: taken as written
to let is to allow or grant
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Funding for a river scheme comes with a flood warning attached.
explanation.definitionFit: An alert is an alarm that tells people of danger.

clue.text: Regretting not taking one step

indicators.note: not taking something means leaving it out, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: to rue is to regret
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone regrets not making a single move.
explanation.definitionFit: A rung is one crossbar on a ladder, the thing you place a foot on to climb.

clue.text: I fish, letting nothing escape, in area with a coast

indicators.note: letting nothing escape means a zero-shaped letter gets out and is lost

blocks.note: taken as written
a sole is a flatfish
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An angler insists no catch gets away along the shoreline.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is an island, land with sea all round it and a shoreline on every side.

clue.text: Installs first of cameras one time, in mysterious Ness

indicators.note: first of points to the opening letter of the next word
something mysterious is puzzling and obscure, so the letters are scrambled
in places the earlier pieces inside the scrambled letters

blocks.note: the opening letter of cameras
once means one time
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone sets up cameras at Loch Ness to catch the mysterious monster.
explanation.walkthrough: Ness is Loch Ness, the Scottish lake of monster fame; here it is only letters to scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensconce is to settle someone or something firmly in place, much as one installs it.

clue.text: Silly bishop returning to embrace witch

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within, so the answer lies inside the run of words
returning means going back, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A foolish cleric runs back to hug a witch.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibyl was a prophetess of the ancient world, and the word is loosely used for a fortune-teller or sorceress.

clue.text: Cheers seeing off first of heavily armoured vehicles

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of the next word
seeing something off means getting rid of it, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: cheers is British slang for thanks
the opening letter of heavily

explanation.surface: A crowd cheers as heavily armoured vehicles roll away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavily armoured' reads as one phrase, but only the H of heavily is used and armoured belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanks are tracked military vehicles protected with thick plating.

clue.text: Smooth attempt to go round one of orbiting bodies

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so this word wraps the next piece

blocks.note: to plane wood is to smooth it
a try is an attempt
a means one

explanation.surface: A smooth effort is made to circle one of the heavenly bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Planetary is the adjective relating to planets, the large bodies that circle a star.
